title: Conservation of Linear Momentum
notes: **Law:** in an isolated system with no external forces, the total linear momentum remains constant.

**Why it is conserved:** Newton's third law gives equal and opposite forces between two bodies. Since $\vec{F}_{12} = -\vec{F}_{21}$, the impulses are equal and opposite, so the total momentum change is zero.
**Collision applications:** in any collision, momentum is always conserved, but kinetic energy is conserved only in elastic collisions.
**Recoil example:** when a gun fires a bullet forward, the gun recoils backward. The momentum of bullet forward equals momentum of gun backward.
